action: wrote rtl/memory/sdram_ctrl.sv (close-page/auto-precharge FSM: powerup/precharge/2xrefresh/MRS init, periodic refresh, picorv32 bus port) and sim/models/sdram_model.sv (behavioral SDR model: command decode, activated-row tracking, CAS-latency read pipeline, byte-masked writes via associative-array backing store); sim/tb/sdram_ctrl_tb.sv
result: First run: 10/14 PASS, 4 FAIL -- all reads returned 'z instead of data. Diagnosed via careful cycle-by-cycle trace: the model's read-data pipeline was CAS_LATENCY+1 deep (should be CAS_LATENCY) AND had an extra registered dq_drive/dq_out stage, adding 2 cycles of latency beyond what the controller actually waits for. Fixed: depth=CAS_LATENCY, dq_drive/dq_out made combinational off index[0]. Rerun: 14/14 PASS, including write/read-back, byte-masked writes, address non-aliasing, and periodic refresh actually firing during normal operation. Explicitly documented the assumed (not datasheet-confirmed) 4-bank/13-row/10-col SDRAM geometry and JEDEC-generic (not manual-sourced) timing parameters in the RTL header comment and docs/known_limitations.md.

action: wrote rtl/peripherals/sd_spi.sv (full SDHC SPI command sequencer: CMD0/CMD8/CMD55+ACMD41(HCS)/CMD58(CCS)/CMD17 with CRC7-signed commands, LBA addressing), sim/models/sdhc_spi_model.sv (SPI slave card model), scripts/{prepare_sd_image,verify_sd_image}.py (versioned raw-sector boot image format), sim/tb/sd_spi_tb.sv
result: Multi-round debugging session, 4 real bugs found and fixed via Animas waveform inspection (query_signals_window/find_signal_transitions), not guesswork: (1) build_cmd used a 6-bit OR ('6'b01_0000|idx') instead of proper 8-bit concatenation for the command byte, corrupting every command's encoding; (2) shift_tx (and thus sd_mosi) updated during the RISING clock phase instead of the FALLING phase, violating SPI mode 0 (data must change on the falling edge); (3) xfer_busy cleared on the SAME rising edge the slave samples the final bit, racing the combinational sd_mosi mux against the slave's sample -- fixed by deferring the busy-clear to the next falling edge; (4) a same-cycle read-after-write hazard checking resp_bytes[4] in the same cycle it was being non-blocking-assigned (same bug class as M1's rf_we issue) -- fixed by checking xfer_rx_byte directly. Also fixed a latent issue in the SDHC model: an early version detected sd_clk edges by registering it in the fast system-clock domain, adding a one-cycle sampling delay relative to the controller's zero-delay bit updates; rewrote the model to clock directly off sd_clk. Final result: 9/9 PASS -- full init handshake (ACMD41 retried exactly twice on purpose, matching the model's designed retry-exercise behavior) plus a CMD17 block read verified byte-for-byte against the known fixture image. Log archived at research/results/m3_sd_spi_tb_final.log
